bl.heroSubtitle: Lift. Reshape. Restore Natural Youthful Contour.
bl.heroDesc1: Breasts naturally change over time. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, weight fluctuations, aging, and gravity can cause the breast tissue to descend, leading to sagging, loss of upper fullness, and downward-pointing nipples. A breast lift is a surgeon-performed procedure designed to elevate and reshape the breasts by removing excess skin and repositioning the breast tissue and nipple for a more youthful, balanced contour.
bl.heroDesc2: At Dr. Soma Plastic Surgery, every breast lift procedure is performed by Dr. Soma, a board-certified plastic surgeon with extensive experience in aesthetic breast surgery. Each plan is tailored to your anatomy, skin quality, and goals, focusing on natural shape, improved symmetry, and safe surgical outcomes.
bl.whatIsDesc1: A breast lift, or <mastopexy>mastopexy</mastopexy>, is a surgical procedure designed to raise and reshape sagging breasts. Major medical institutions such as the <mayo>Mayo Clinic</mayo> describe breast lift surgery as a method to raise and reshape breasts when changes from aging, pregnancy, or weight fluctuations cause sagging.
bl.whatIsDesc2: It involves removing excess stretched skin, repositioning breast tissue to a higher position, and elevating the nipple and areola to a natural level.
bl.nippleElevDesc: Repositions downward-pointing nipples to a youthful level.
bl.skinReductionDesc: Removes excess stretched skin envelope for firmness.
bl.ptosisDesc: Breasts naturally change over time due to various factors. Sagging is common, normal, and treatable.
bl.cause1Desc: Loss of fat volume causes deflation.
bl.cause2Desc: Loss of skin elasticity over time.
bl.howDesc: Dr. Soma prioritizes natural breast proportions, stable nipple positioning, and long-term shape support.
bl.step0Desc: Detailed measurements, symmetry planning, and marking the breast shape.
bl.step1Desc: Carefully chosen pattern based on the degree of sagging and skin quality.
bl.step2Desc: Removing excess skin, reshaping tissue, and repositioning the nipple/areola.
bl.step3Desc: Layered closure for internal support, followed by dressings and surgical bra.
bl.typesDesc: The best technique depends on the degree of sagging, breast size, and skin quality.
bl.type0Desc: Best for mild sagging. Incision around the areola. Can reduce areola size. Minimal scarring pattern.
bl.type1Desc: Best for moderate sagging. Incision around areola plus a vertical line to crease. Stronger reshaping and projection.
bl.type2Desc: Best for significant sagging or heavier breasts. Greatest lift and skin removal. Excellent for major reshaping.
bl.type3Desc: For lifted breasts plus more volume. Enhances upper pole fullness. Best when volume loss is a major concern.
bl.imp0Imp: Elevates downward-pointing nipples to natural height
bl.imp1Imp: Can reduce stretched areolas for better proportion
bl.imp2Imp: Creates a firmer, rounder, more youthful shape
bl.imp3Imp: Balances uneven sagging between both breasts
bl.imp4Imp: Improves projection (add implants if volume is low)
bl.evidenceDesc: The surgical principles behind mastopexy are well established in aesthetic plastic surgery literature.
bl.auth0Desc: Explains breast lift surgery as a method to change breast shape and raise breasts by removing excess skin.
bl.auth1Desc: Discusses how breast shape and firmness change due to aging, gravity, and pregnancy, and how surgery restores contour.
bl.auth2Desc: Clinical studies evaluating mastopexy techniques, scar patterns, and complication rates supporting safe surgical planning.
bl.rec0Desc: Support bra applied. Mild soreness. Return to desk work (comfort dependent). Avoid lifting.
bl.rec1Desc: Swelling reduces. Bruising improves. Light walking encouraged. Support bra continues.
bl.rec2Desc: Resume light exercise (with approval). Shape appears more settled. Scars begin to mature.
bl.rec3Desc: Final contour becomes more natural. Scars continue to fade. Full shape refinement.
bl.painDesc: "Tightness and soreness similar to chest muscle fatigue." - Most patients describe it as discomfort rather than sharp pain.
bl.cand1: Stable weight and good overall health.
bl.cand2: Non-smoker or willing to stop temporarily.
bl.notSuitableDesc: Pregnant/breastfeeding, uncontrolled medical conditions, major weight changes expected, or smoking without willingness to stop.
bl.ben0: Restores youthful breast height and contour
bl.ben2: Elevates nipple position for natural appearance

bl.faqDesc: Clear answers to help you make informed decisions
bl.faq0A: A breast lift (mastopexy) is a surgical procedure that lifts and reshapes sagging breasts by removing excess skin and repositioning the nipple and breast tissue.
bl.faq1Q: How is a breast lift done?
bl.faq1A: Incisions are made based on the degree of sagging, excess skin is removed, breast tissue is reshaped, and the nipple and areola are repositioned to a higher, natural level.
bl.faq2A: You will notice an immediate lift, but swelling takes time to settle. Most patients see a more stable shape at 4-6 weeks, with final refinement from 3-6 months.
bl.faq3Q: How long does a breast lift last?
bl.faq3A: Results are long-lasting, but aging, gravity, pregnancy, and weight changes can affect the breasts over time. Stable weight and good support help maintain results.
bl.faq4Q: Does a breast lift make breasts bigger?
bl.faq4A: A breast lift primarily reshapes and elevates. It can make breasts appear fuller due to improved positioning, but it does not add volume. For larger size, implants can be combined.
bl.faq5A: Discomfort is usually mild to moderate in the first week and is controlled with medication. Most patients describe tightness rather than sharp pain.
bl.faq6Q: Can I breastfeed after a lift?
bl.faq6A: Many patients can breastfeed, depending on the technique and tissue changes. This is discussed during consultation based on your future plans.
bl.faq7Q: Does a breast lift leave scars?
bl.faq7A: Yes, but incision placement is planned to be as discreet as possible. Scars fade significantly over time with proper aftercare and scar management.
bl.faq8A: When performed by a certified plastic surgeon in a proper medical facility, breast lift surgery is generally safe. Risks exist like all surgeries and are explained during consultation.
bl.faq9Q: What happens if I get pregnant after?
bl.faq9A: Pregnancy can stretch breast skin and affect the lifted shape. If pregnancy is planned soon, it may be better to delay surgery for longer-lasting results.
